newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares trim gains after setting record high.
newsitem.headline: German shares trim gains after setting record high.

text.p: The German DAX index of top shares, after surging past 2,900 points in bourse trading for the first time ever, pared gains in Thursday electronic trading under the weight of a weakened dollar and falling bonds.
The blue-chip index closed IBIS dealings at 2,894.43, up 13.54 points, or 0.47 percent, as the dollar slipped off 23-month highs reached on Tuesday and dropped under 1.55 marks.
Earlier in the day, the DAX finished floor trading up 43.84 points at a record close of 2,909.91 points, just shy of the day's bourse high of 2,914.61 and the IBIS high of 2,916.16.
"When Bunds and the dollar went down, they took stocks with them," one Frankfurt trader said.
Friday's outlook would depend heavily on the dollar's overnight direction and on Wall Street, dealers said.
After two successive day's of losses, the Dow Jones index was down 14.16 points to 6,408.78 by 1625 GMT.
The DAX rally to new highs surprised experts who had predicted profit-taking would hold off another run at the magical 2,900 mark for at least another several trading sessions.

A jump in German bonds, spurred by a rise in unemployment, sparked the DAX climb. Bunds rose as much as 30 basis points as the unemployment figures had lifted hopes the Bundesbank would ease its stance against rate cuts.

Germany added 50,000 to seasonally adjusted unemployment rolls in November, lifting the total number to 4.1 million. The adjusted joblessness rate rose to 10.7 percent, up from 10.1 percent in October.
Stocks scaled back when Bunds fell after the Bundesbank said it would leave key rates unchanged. In late dealings Bunds lost even more ground as U.S. Treasuries tumbled steeply.
Industrial group Mannesmann AG, which had soared on rumour of a telecommunications alliance with utility Veba AG, pared back gains to close electronic trading at 673 marks, up 4.20.
Export-driven stocks were hurt most by the dollar's drop. Car maker BMW AG stood at an IBIS close of 1,050 marks, down 19.30, after trading as high as 1,089 during the day.
Traders on Thursday had been ready for a restrained trading after two days of Wall Street setbacks, and questioned whether the DAX could maintain its lofty level at record highs.
"I am skeptical. We need a consolidation. I must warn that it's not institutional investors who are leading this rally," said one Frankfurt trader.
